newsitem.title: UK: UK's Blair says will attend Hong Kong handover.
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair says will attend Hong Kong handover.

text.p: British Prime Minister Tony Blair ended weeks of speculation on Wednesday and confirmed he would be attending the ceremony to mark the handover of Hong Kong to China at midnight on June 30.

Blair, asked in parliament whether Britain owed a moral duty to the people of Hong Kong which would not end with the handover ceremony, told the House of Commons: "I do agree...I think that is important ... I will be attending the ceremony myself."
The Labour government, swept to power in an election landslide on May 1, has said it will continue to put pressure on Beijing to respect human rights in Hong Kong after the handover.

The handover has been overshadowed by criticism from Britain and its Western allies of China's plans for an unelected legislature to replace Hong Kong's Legislative Council returned by about one million voters in a 1995 poll.
The United States snubbed China on Tuesday by announcing that Secretary of State Madeleine Albright would boycott the investiture of the unelected legislature at the handover gala.

Speculation had been rife that Blair might shun the event altogether. The Foreign Office said earlier on Wednesday: "The government's position on the provisional legislature is well known. There has never been any question of British ministers attending the swearing-in of a provisional legislature chosen by a hand-picked body of 400."
